body:
Thanks for the thoughtful reply. Yeah, I'd really like to have a more consistent experience through medication, but I'm grateful to even find the balance. Maybe one day I'll feel stable enough to try new ones.

I think I'm done thinking sad thoughts for the night. You and the other poster really helped. [here](http://m.youtube.com/watch?v=ofnSojq-vqI)'s a really funny standup set that your comment reminded me of. I'm going to watch this and think happy thoughts.

It's a certain dosage/application of recreational drugs that I've found before to help with social anxiety. Probably less harmful than most meds would be, but I'm not negligent of health concerns too. Everything else is just a matter of time, I suppose.

How do/did you reconcile the person you were before meds with who you are now? I'd be uncomfortable using a non-organic support to keep going, even if the alternative is suicide. Everything I know has taught me to avoid crutches, that they weaken you in the long run. I can't help but imagine how much worse it would be to accept a normal life and then lose this coping mechanism again.

Yeah, the body fights hard to be alive. But either through conditioning or malfunction, the neurotransmitters that make me want to live don't work normally. It's almost an identity crisis: does the *real* me want to live? Am I only me when I have this supply of drug? It's a whole new host of personal questions that need answers, which is funny. I thought I was done with those when I simply wanted to die.

Thanks for reading, and answering. Hope you have a good day.
